text:
maria: Heads up — after pushing the base-image rebase (ubuntu:22.04 + glibc bump) we started seeing GPU containers fail to find / run against libcuda on a subset of hosts in eu-central.
lee: Can you paste the failing logs? is it a mount error or missing symbols?
maria: Short log from a failed job on node gpu-eu-12:
```
Failed to load libnvidia-ml.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
CUDA error: unknown error (cuInit failed)
container start: devices: []
/proc/driver/nvidia: no such file or directory
```
sam: That looks like the host driver isn't exposing devices into the container (nvidia libs not bind-mounted). Did the rebase change nvidia-container-runtime/nvidia-ctk?
maria: We upgraded nvidia-container-toolkit to 1.12 on the image and dropped a shim that used to create host symlinks. Hosts with older kernel+driver combos (470.xx) are affected.
dinesh: Interesting — only eu-central? us-west seems fine. Could be host driver versions differ between zones.
lee: Checked host probe on gpu-eu-12: `modinfo nvidia` OK, driver present. But `ps -ef | grep nvidia` shows daemon not started. udev rules look different after the image change — the init container we use relies on the host path /usr/lib/nvidia to be there.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1123 (gpu-lib-probe-failure) — pages: oncall
maria: Repro steps for local dev: run the same image on a host with 470 driver -> inside container `ls /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-*.so*` returns nothing. On hosts with 525 driver it works.
sam: Sounds like the new toolkit expects libnvidia symlinks at different path and falls back to probing /proc/driver/nvidia which isn't populated when drivers aren't loaded in the host namespace the same way.
lee: Quick mitigation: add hostPath mounts to the pod spec (temporary) for /usr/lib/nvidia and /proc/driver/nvidia in the node-drainer DaemonSet to keep jobs running. But we need infra approval to rollout.
ops: If we drain nodes to restart kubelet/init, we risk losing 10% capacity in eu for the afternoon. Jobs queued: ~1200 GPU hours pending. Cost impact estimate: ~ $3k/day if backlog delays push up burst usage.
dinesh: Plan: 1) revert base-image to previous tag for critical pools (canary on 5 nodes) 2) push a small init-container that creates the missing symlinks and bind-mounts as fallback 3) schedule controlled node reboots for hosts with older drivers 4) long term pin toolkit version or roll host driver upgrade.
maria: I'm starting the revert to base-image:v2026.02 on the dedicated pool now — will watch canary jobs.
lee: I have a small patch to the init-container that checks for `/proc/driver/nvidia` and runs `modprobe nvidia` if missing, plus creates `ln -s` for libnvidia* into /usr/lib. Pushing as image `infra-helper:rev3`.
infra-bot: Deploy plan scheduled: canary revert at 2026-03-18T16:30Z, full revert at 18:00Z if canary green.
sam: Also opened a ticket with NVIDIA support — linking driver/kernel mismatch hypothesis: some older drivers don't export the same soname locations expected by toolkit 1.12.
ops: Please add a note to the status page if we hit broader customer impact. Keep me posted on the drain schedule.
dinesh: I'll coordinate with node team to avoid draining more than 2 nodes at once in eu-central during business hours.
maria: Update 16:40Z — canary revert succeeded, 4/5 jobs that were failing are now running. Still seeing 1 host with persistent `/proc/driver/nvidia` missing; isolating that node.
lee: For follow-up: we should add a preflight probe in our image deploy pipeline that runs a quick `ldconfig && ldd $(which nvidia-smi) | grep libnvidia` check against real host kernel/driver matrix.
maria: Agreed. I'll create a postmortem stub and link the actions: revert, init-fallback, preflight check, driver upgrade schedule.
ops: Thanks — please ping oncall if anything regresses. :eyes:
